reviewedFrom: Posting-status integrity: a source document reports 'posted' only when its current economic revision is in the ledger; an economic change shows as pending until reprojected and then supersedes the prior entry (reversed, not deleted); a non-economic edit never adds money; a replacement that cannot post leaves the prior monetary history in place and surfaces a finding that leads back to the source; the repair resolves exactly that finding. Amounts are integer cents.

bill-harmless-edit.derivation: Changing a due date is not an accounting event: no new journal, no reversal, status current after projection.

bill-economic-edits.derivation: An approved bill's total is fixed (corrections go through credits), so its economic edits are re-coding and the accounting date: cost code, job, expense account and bill date. Each is pending until reprojected, then the prior entry is reversed and a replacement posted. Final: 1,000 on the second job, second cost code, expense account 5020, dated July 20.

bill-closed-period-replacement-and-repai.derivation: July is closed. Re-coding the July bill to expense account 5020 must not post into July and must not retire the posted 1,000 in 5000: either the edit is refused, or the bill shows blocked with a finding that names it. Reopening July and reprojecting posts the re-coded bill, resolves the finding and July closes again.

expense-family.derivation: A 500 job expense paid from operating cash posts Dr 5000 / Cr 1000 once approved. Re-coding its line to another cost code is pending until reprojected, then supersedes the entry. Rejecting it retires the posting: the entry is reversed, the ledger is empty and the expense reads 'reversed', never 'pending' or 'posted'.

invoice-view-and-revision.derivation: A client viewing an issued invoice changes nothing economic: no new entries and the status is current after projection. Revising it voids the original (its posting reversed, never deleted) and the reissued replacement posts once at 1,200; the voided original reads 'reversed' (it carries no money), never 'pending' or 'posted'.

partial-run-scoped-resolution.derivation: Two July bills are re-coded while July is closed, so both are blocked with findings. After reopening, a projection run scoped to bill A resolves only bill A's finding; bill B stays blocked and its finding open — a partial run never reports the rest of the company clean. A full run then resolves bill B.
